topicName: Graph Databases and Property Graph Models
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Graph Databases and Property Graph Models"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Graph databases represent a paradigm shift in database design, moving away from rigid tabular structures to connected networks of data. This tutorial explores the fundamentals of graph databases and the Property Graph Model."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Introduction to Graph Databases"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Traditional relational databases excel at structured, tabular data but struggle with deeply connected information, requiring expensive JOIN operations. Graph databases are designed to treat relationships as first-class citizens, allowing for high-performance traversal across highly interconnected datasets."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"The Property Graph Model"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"The most popular formalism for graph databases is the Labeled Property Graph (LPG) model. An LPG consists of nodes, relationships, properties, and labels."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Nodes: Entities or objects in the graph, equivalent to rows in relational tables or documents in document stores."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Relationships: Directed connections between two nodes that provide context and semantic meaning."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Properties: Key-value pairs stored on both nodes and relationships to hold descriptive data."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Labels: Tags used to group nodes into categories, improving query performance and organization."},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Designing a Property Graph"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"When designing a property graph, you must map your domain entities to nodes and their interactions to relationships. Consider an e-commerce domain where users purchase products and write reviews."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"CREATE (u:User {id: '1', name: 'Alice'})-[:PURCHASED {date: '2023-10-01'}]->(p:Product {id: '100', title: 'Laptop'})"},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"Querying with Cypher"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"Graph databases utilize specialized query languages. Cypher is a declarative graph query language that uses pattern-matching syntax to traverse the graph visually."},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"MATCH (u:User {name: 'Alice'})-[:PURCHASED]->(p:Product) RETURN p.title"},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices for Graph Database Design"},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Avoid anti-patterns like using node properties as relationship stand-ins."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Keep relationship types action-oriented (e.g., FOLLOWS, PURCHASED, LIKES)."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Index frequently queried node properties to speed up the starting points of graph traversals."}]
